text: Meanwhile, Magadha kept growing. Its new rulers, the Nanda kings, were famous for two things,
a gigantic army, and an even bigger treasury. And far to the west, a young king from Macedonia
had just conquered the mightiest empire in the world, Persia. He wanted more. His name
was Alexander. In 326 BCE, Alexander crossed into the Punjab. On the banks of the Jaylam
River, he fought a king called Porus, whose army brought something the Greeks had rarely
faced, war elephants. Alexander won, but the Greek writers tell a famous story about what
came next. How do you wish to be treated? Like a king. Hmm, fair. Keep your kingdom. Then
Alexander pushed east to the river Bias, and there his army simply stopped. They had marched
for eight years. They had heard about the Nanda army waiting beyond, thousands of elephants,
hundreds of thousands of soldiers, and the monsoon rain would not stop. They refused
to go any further. Alexander, who had never lost a battle, had to turn back.
Undefeated, except by his own tired soldiers, and the weather. Alexander died in Babylon
three years later at 32 he never saw India again but a young man in India had
